main_text.l: ordium, Narratio, Propositio, Confirmatio, Con-
futatio, & Peroratio. Exordium est orationis princi-
pium, animum auditoris ad reliqua praeparans. Eius fines
sunt tres, Benevolentia, Attentio, Docilitas: quae petun-
tur a rebus, vel personis, idq; ex locis inueniendis Logicae.
1. v. 1. 10. Rom. 9. v. 1. c. 10. v. 1. Narratio est rei gestae expositio.
Itaque exordio statim subiicitur, si propositio sit inde ded-
ucenda; vel praemittitur ei propositio, si hanc declarare pos-
sit. Exempla vide Act. 2. v. 22. & seqq. c. 22. v. 3. Apoc. 1. v. 9. &
seqq. Propositio est, quae continet thema & summam oratio-
nis. Illa si fuerit multiplex, partitio dicitur. Ratio autem in
plures quam tres vel quatuor partes debet diuidi. Exem-
plum partitionis est Apoc. 1. v. 19. Scribe quae vidisti, & quae sunt,
& post haec futura sunt. Quibus verbis apocalypsis diuiditur
in duo summa capita, videl. tractationem rerum praesentium
& futurarum. Confirmatio est argumentorum deductio: vt ne
pe propositio recte persuaderi possit. Confutatio est contra-
riorum argumentorum solutio. Quae confirmationi prae-
mittitur, si auditor sit occupatus insigni praeiudicio. V-
triusque exemplum vide 1. Cor. 15. Peroratio est artificiosus
terminus orationis. In hac vt plurimum est ἀναχεφαλαίωσις
& παθοποιΐα, h.e. recapitulatio & affectuum concitatio.
Vide Philip. 4. v. 1. & seqq. Hebr. 13. v. 20. 21. In confutatione
peculiares quidam modi adhibentur: puta regestio Rom. 9.

page.notes: The marginal numerals 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 are printed line counters, not text, so they are left out. Greek words (ἀναχεφαλαίωσις, παθοποιΐα, μίμησις) are copied as far as legible and may contain small errors; the first Greek word in particular should be checked. The phrase "ne pe propositio" is printed with a split word at the line end and is kept as printed. "eode stratagemate" is printed as "eode ftrata-gemate", with the long s read as s. The phrase "ex locis inueniendis" was read as "ex locis inuentionis" in the scan; the printed form appears to be "inuentionis" and is kept as such. Printing errors such as "Sam. 13." for 1. Sam. are left as printed.
